# container.Base#createItem drops an item config's own theme: the object branch assigns the class default or the parent's over it, while the class branch keeps it

## Problem

A container item declared as a config object with its own `theme` never gets it. `src/container/Base.mjs#createItem`, object branch:

```js
item.theme = defaults.theme || module.config.theme || me.theme
```

The right-hand side never consults `item.theme`, so an explicit `theme: 'neo-theme-neo-light'` on an item config under a dark parent is overwritten with the class default (usually `null`) or the parent's theme. The class branch a few lines above keeps it — `Neo.create({theme: item.config.theme || me.theme, ...defaults, module: item, ...config})` spreads the instance config last — so the two ways of declaring the same item disagree.

Nested themes are the documented feature ("a dark-themed grid inside a light-themed panel" in the styling guide), and a child carrying its own theme is how the shared tooltip decides which theme class to stamp on itself (`component.Base#getTheme` walks the parents' classes).

## Evidence

Measured on a component fixture (2026-09-02 14:53Z, `dev@4e0e9dd8c3`): a `Container` item config with `theme: 'neo-theme-neo-light'` inside a viewport under `neo-theme-neo-dark` rendered with classes `neo-container neo-flex-container …` — no theme class — and `Neo.worker.App.getConfigs({id, keys: ['theme']})` on its button read `[null]`; hovering that button stamped `neo-theme-neo-dark` on the shared tooltip. The same fixture with the theme moved to a subclass's class config (`module.config.theme`) renders the class and stamps the light theme.

- `src/container/Base.mjs:400–405` (class branch, instance config wins) vs `:452` (object branch, instance config overwritten).
- The line's origin: #6637 made class-config themes win over the parent's during `createItem` — it never considered an explicit item theme.

## Change

`item.theme = item.theme || defaults.theme || module.config.theme || me.theme` in the object branch — an explicit item config outranks `itemDefaults`, the class default and the parent, in that order, which is the precedence every other item config key already has.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit: a container under a dark theme creating `{module: Component, theme: 'neo-theme-neo-light'}` yields a child whose `theme` is the light one and whose `cls` carries it; red on `dev`.
- [ ] Unit: a child without its own theme still receives `itemDefaults.theme`, then the class default, then the parent's — unchanged precedence for the existing cases.
- [ ] Lazy-loaded items (`module` as a loader function) keep their current path.

## Non-goals

- The functional component path (`examples/functional/hostComponent/Component.mjs` sets a theme on a vdom child) — a different creation route, not measured here.
- The value-sheet weight question (#18102), which surfaced this while building its witness.
